modelName: Whatcom coop as a value network — roles, deliverables, and what never comes back
modelNote: Verna Allee's Value Network Analysis drawn in RCN house style. Nodes are ROLES, not people — 'CHW' is one node though six people do the job. Every arrow carries a deliverable label: the thing that actually moves. Solid arrows are tangible (contractual product and revenue); dashed arrows are intangible (knowledge, trust, information, benefit). Red dotted arrows are Allee's exchange-analysis finding: a return that ought to exist and does not. Built 2026-08-31 with Marc Pierson from the Snowden/Allee research thread. PROVENANCE: nothing in this file is measured. Every arrow is asserted from the Snowden/Allee research thread and general knowledge of CHW programmes. The household money arrow (payroll share, copay) was deliberately omitted to sharpen the counterflow reading and should be restored if it exists. IAD LEVEL: operational (asserted 2026-08-31, open to correction at the Ostrom Workshop). Care, money and knowledge exchanged between roles — choices here directly affect tangible outcomes. The two red arrows are not operational findings at all: "no seat in plan design" says the CHW position has no adjacency to a COLLECTIVE-CHOICE arena, which in Ostrom terms is a boundary-rule exclusion.

legendEntries.label: A role — what gets done here, not who does it
The role the whole network exists to serve
A RETURN THAT ISN'T THERE — asserted, needs checking

nodes.label: Value converts only when the other role ACCEPTS it. And nothing on this canvas is measured — it is a structure to argue with.
nodes.note: Two separate warnings. The first is Allee: offering is not delivering. The second is provenance: every arrow here was reasoned out, not observed. Deliberate omission worth overruling — member households almost certainly pay a payroll share or a copay, and that arrow was left out to sharpen the counterflow reading. If it belongs, put it back; it weakens the finding below and that is exactly what it should do.

nodes.label: REINSURER
nodes.note: Carries the catastrophic tail the coop cannot absorb. Purely contractual: premium out, cover back. No intangible arrows touch it at all, which is exactly right — it is the one role that needs to know nothing about Whatcom.

nodes.label: EMPLOYER
nodes.note: Pays. Does not receive care and does not decide clinically. In Allee's terms it is a pure tangible-out role with one intangible input — being told why its premium moved.

nodes.label: CO-OP
nodes.note: Where the deciding is done. Receives premium, pays capitation, wage and reinsurance. Every tangible arrow in the drawing passes through here — which is the definition of a bottleneck, and also the reason the coop is worth building.

nodes.label: CLINIC
nodes.note: Delivers care and explanation. Receives capitation from the coop and situational knowledge from the CHW. Returns nothing to the CHW — see the red arrow.

nodes.label: MEMBER HOUSEHOLD
nodes.note: Receives care, rides and explanation. Gives lived experience and trust. Notice what is absent: NOT ONE money arrow touches this node. The person receiving the service is entirely outside the money circuit.

nodes.label: CHW
nodes.note: One role, six people. Extends three intangibles — trust to the household, situational knowledge to the clinic, failure reports to the coop — and receives one wage and one intangible back. This is the asymmetry the drawing exists to make visible.

nodes.label: The one who pays, the one who decides and the one who receives are three different roles.
nodes.note: Odum's counterflow reading. Follow the amber circuit: Employer to Coop to Clinic. Follow the green circuit: Clinic to Household. They do not close on each other. In a normal market those two circuits are the same loop between two parties; here they are separate shapes, and every design problem in health finance lives in that gap.

nodes.label: Reciprocity: the CHW extends three intangibles and gets one back. That is a burnout shape, not a score.
nodes.note: Allee's exchange-analysis question, verbatim: is one of the roles extending several intangibles without receiving a similar return? You read it off the arrowheads. No centrality metric was computed and none is needed — which is the whole argument for drawing roles rather than surveying people.

edges.label: premium
edges.note: The money enters here and only here.

edges.label: capitation
edges.note: Paid per member per month rather than per service — which is what lets the clinic afford the green arrow to the household without counting visits.

edges.label: wage
edges.note: The only return the CHW receives for three extended intangibles.

edges.label: care delivered
edges.note: The green circuit. Note it never returns to the payer — the household has no money arrow to give back.

edges.label: rides, forms, follow-up
edges.note: Tangible and unglamorous. Getting somebody to dialysis is a delivered good, not a soft benefit. Drawn separately from the trust arrow because the two fail independently: a CHW can keep delivering rides long after the trust is gone, and vice versa.

edges.label: trust, translation, advocacy
edges.note: The deliverable that makes the other five arrows in this corner possible, and the one nobody can be assigned to produce. It was missing from the first cut of this drawing, which made the reciprocity claim overstate itself by one arrow.

edges.label: catastrophic cover
edges.note: The counterflow return on m3. This pair is the only fully closed tangible loop in the drawing.

edges.label: lived experience, trust
edges.note: The household's only outbound deliverable, and it is the most valuable thing in the network.

edges.label: what's actually going on at home
edges.note: The deliverable the clinic cannot buy and cannot generate. This arrow is why the CHW role exists.

edges.label: where the system fails people
edges.note: Failure reports from the edge. Whether the coop acts on them is a separate question — see x2.

edges.label: explanation, reassurance
edges.note: Drawn separately from 'care delivered' on purpose. They are different deliverables and they fail independently.

edges.label: why the premium moved
edges.note: The employer's only intangible input. Thin, and the whole renewal conversation rests on it.

edges.label: no clinical follow-back
edges.note: ASSERTED, NOT OBSERVED. Derived from Allee exchange analysis, not from anything measured in Whatcom. The claim is that the CHW tells the clinic what is happening at home and hears nothing back about what was done with it. Check it before believing it.

edges.label: no seat in plan design
edges.note: ASSERTED, NOT OBSERVED. The claim is that the role which knows where the system fails has no arrow into how the system is designed. If a CHW does sit in plan design, delete this arrow — it is the cheapest one to disprove and the most expensive one to be wrong about.
